Employee onboarding flowchart

From the accepted offer to the 30-day review, with four parties. A starting point for HR teams that want the same process for everyone.

Open this flow in the editor Free, no sign-up. Opens as a new diagram in your browser.
The flow: Employee onboarding
Interactive diagram: drag to pan, scroll to zoom. Changes made here are not saved.

How to read the flow

  1. It starts when the offer is accepted: HR sends the contract and asks for the documents.
  2. The first decision holds the process until the documents are complete before day one; if something is missing, HR chases it and checks again.
  3. The manager prepares the first-week plan and assigns a buddy.
  4. IT creates the accounts and prepares the laptop before the person arrives.
  5. On day one the new hire collects the laptop, signs in and completes the mandatory training.
  6. At 30 days the manager decides whether things are on track. If not, they agree a support plan and review again.

The text behind the diagram

This is what Diagramico exports under Export → AI text. It also works the other way round: paste this text into Diagrams → Import text and the diagram is drawn.

DIAGRAM: Employee onboarding

LANES:
HR = Human Resources (department)
MG = Manager (person)
IT = IT (team)
NH = New hire (person)

NODES:
HR1 start: Offer accepted
HR2 step: Sends the contract and asks for the documents
HR3 decision: Documents complete before day one?
HR4 step: Chases the missing documents
MG1 step: Prepares the first-week plan and assigns a buddy
IT1 step: Creates the accounts and prepares the laptop
NH1 user_action: Day one: collects the laptop and signs in
NH2 user_action: Completes the mandatory training
MG2 decision: 30-day review: on track?
MG3 step: Agrees a support plan
HR5 end: Onboarding complete

FLOW:
HR1 > HR2 > HR3
HR3 > MG1 [yes]
HR3 > HR4 [no]
HR4 > HR3
MG1 > IT1 > NH1 > NH2 > MG2
MG2 > HR5 [yes]
MG2 > MG3 [no]
MG3 > MG2

Ask an AI

Each button copies the request together with the flow text. Paste it into the assistant you use.

Documentation

Write the documentation of this process for the people who will run it: purpose, who takes part, numbered steps by owner and what happens at each decision. Use only what is in the flow and point out anything that is not defined.

Test cases

List the test cases for this process as a table: scenario, starting condition, steps and expected result. Cover every branch of every decision, including the ones that loop back.

Review the logic

Review the logic of this process. Point out decisions with no way out, loops that may never end, steps with no clear owner and cases the flow does not handle. Do not rewrite the process: list the problems by severity.

Adapt it to your case

  • Add a lane for the buddy if they have tasks of their own.
  • For remote work, replace collecting the laptop with a shipping step and a confirmation of receipt.
  • Use a note on the 30-day review to write down the criteria the manager checks.
